analysis.title: Charts at Goldman Sachs 02.11.2026 (Johannes Duttenhoefer, FICC & Equities)
key_insights: Prediction markets imply more than 90% odds that Democrats win the House and more than 65% that they win the Senate in the US midterms (Kalshi, Polymarket).

GS expects data centers as a campaign theme to fade after the midterms because the issue ranks low among voter priorities. Congress might limit data center tax incentives, but a national moratorium looks unlikely.
GS expects significant data center growth acceleration in both US national and key regional power markets in 2026/27.
Global data center GPU power demand is expected to rise from 13,510MW in 2025 to 150,081MW in 2030, a CAGR of +62%.
Congress will likely need to raise the debt limit no later than October 2027.
Voters rank cost of living as the most important issue facing them. AI is the top issue for only 2% of voters (Harris Poll).
Long-dated oil prices (Brent) have risen significantly since September.
The AI labor market impact is spreading beyond the Technology sector, based on layoff data.
October saw the largest drop in global risk appetite since November 2021 (GS Risk Appetite Indicator).
S&P 500 52-week market breadth remains negative, below 1 standard deviation.
October and November are historically among the prime months for corporate share repurchases.
Korea's semiconductor memory sector trades at record low forward P/E levels, which GS reads as the market's lack of conviction in earnings sustainability.
In China, high-tech sectors sustain a sizable growth contribution as the property drag gradually diminishes.
GS raised its global robot shipment forecasts by more than 4x a few months ago, and Meta is also entering robotics. Robot costs are set to decline 7% annually.
S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth is tracking at 33% y/y, but the size of beats versus estimates is smaller than in Q1 and Q2.
The S&P 500 excluding AI stocks has risen alongside the sell-off in AI stocks.
Consensus estimates show hyperscaler free cash flow declining further in 2027 and rebounding in 2028.

GS estimates AI financing needs may be less than investors expect: about $65bn through FY28 to support about $180bn of capex (offset by about $35bn of prepayments and $80bn of operating cash flow). Oracle needs about $20bn of capital against $220bn of capex, offset by about $110bn of vendor financing, BYOH and prepayments.
Semiconductor company revenues are projected to rise to $872bn (annualized, vs. 2022, consensus) by end-2026.

24.6% of firms use AI in regular business functions (+0.8pp from September), and 28.6% expect to use it in the next 6 months (Census Bureau). Adoption is approaching 50% in the Information, Professional and Finance sectors.
The North America Consumer Health Indicator stands around P50 in the US and P40 in Canada.
Higher bond yields are likely to weigh on global GDP growth.
Prediction market volumes have grown substantially in 2026.
The US personal saving rate has declined.
Equity demand from the wealthiest households has likely benefited from liquid wealth created by large public offerings, and GS expects this to remain a tailwind in coming quarters.

sector_views.rationale: AI stocks sold off while the S&P 500 ex AI rose. Semiconductor revenues are projected at $872bn annualized by end-2026, and GS expects significant data center power demand growth.
Memory sector trades at record low forward P/E, which GS reads as low market conviction in earnings sustainability.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth is tracking at 33% y/y (FactSet, GS). This is a tracking figure for a season still in progress, not a final result.
S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS has exceeded estimates by a smaller magnitude than in Q1 and Q2 2026.
Consensus estimates (FactSet) show hyperscaler free cash flow declining further in 2027 and rebounding in 2028.

Oracle's capital need is about $20bn, with $220bn of capex offset by about $110bn of vendor financing, BYOH and prepayments, versus GS's estimate of about $65bn of financing needs through FY28 for about $180bn of capex.
